title: XTP, service, planner, Storage and provisioning ownership
summary: Applications request a named service; Service Descriptor Registry supplies class/peer/point; Operational Planner supplies admission and resource share; transport and fabric enforce native capabilities only; provisioning is an independently authorised management service.
invariants: Application traffic cannot self-assign operational class or critical priority
Service identity never contains IP/MAC/UDP carrier fields
Service Registry is not a cryptographic identity provider
Storage owns object/range coordinates and source fan-in; XTP owns reliability, sequence, route, pacing
Queue Fabric, JSON-RPC and direct call are alternative application connector choices and cannot be forced to depend on XTP
XTP route provisioning must not invent a second carrier selector, endpoint authority or multicast authentication scheme
procedure: Resolve service name to registered class, logical route peer and point
Get a planner decision for resource domain and state
Ask XTP RouteTable for carrier/path only after service and policy decisions
Treat range verified bytes as storage-owned independent of XTP context lifetime
